summary: When a worn ESP amulet is polymorphed into another amulet, C removes the old item, installs the replacement in the same slot, and reapplies wear effects. The JS poly_obj caller skips accessory removal and set_wear, so setworn tries to replace the still-worn amulet with an environment that lacks cancelDoff and throws. The ordinary scan reproduces this at js/zap.js:2546 through potion_dip. The C trace diverges at zero-based step 173 after matching through step 172.

source.branch: Inventory polymorph when old_wornmask includes W_AMUL and wearslot(replacement) preserves W_AMUL; remove the old worn item before assigning the replacement, then call set_wear and reread the slot.

evidence: nethack-c/upstream/src/zap.c:1929-1949 unconditionally calls remove_worn_item(obj, TRUE), then setworn(otmp, new_wornmask), set_wear(otmp), and wearmask_to_obj(new_wornmask) for a nonzero replacement mask. The JS poly_obj implementation at js/zap.js:2518-2546 excludes W_AMUL from that call and throws before the next boundary.

nethack-c/upstream/src/steal.c:213-290 implements remove_worn_item: W_AMUL calls Amulet_off(), then any remaining worn bits go through setnotworn(). do_wear.c:1642-1659 requires cancel_doff() as part of worn-slot changes. js/steal.js:375 currently calls setnotworn(obj, { state }), dropping the hooks from its environment; preserve the do_wear hook environment when enabling this path for other amulet types.

nethack-c/upstream/src/potion.c:2442-2492 calls poly_obj from potion_dip for polymorphing the dipped object. The synthetic input exercises that production path with a worn ESP amulet and a polymorph potion.

The ordinary baseline diagnostic is .cache/A2-v64-worn-amulet-poly-scan.json at replay commit 4c0954db711c705152053bc79650fc35208886a0. It reports the error through potion_dip -> poly_obj -> setworn: worn requires cancelDoff for otyp 201. The accepted v64 manifest records the C step 173 boundary and an observational match through step 172.
